title.narrative: Access to CSE in Sub-Saharan Africa Project
Tillgång till omfattande SexualitetInformationutbildning i söder om AfrikProject

description.narrative: Projektet "Barnens tillgång till omfattande sexual informationen och utbildning i Afrika söder om Sahara" av Rädda Barnen syftar till att nå 336.000 barn (28.000) i 12 mottagarländer. Interventionen syftar till att förbättra ungdomars tillgång till omfattande sexualundervisning genom att förbättra partnerorganisationernas förmåga att ge och förespråkar för barns tillgång till CSE i regionen

The project 'Children's access to comprehensive sexuality information & education in sub-saharan Africa' by Save the Children seeks to reach 336,000 children (28,000) in 12 target countries. The intervention seeks to improve young people's access to comprehensive sexuality education by improving the partner organisations' capacity to provide and advocate for children's access to CSE in the region.

General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2016Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: The intended outcome of the project was that 340,000 children under the age of eighteen (18) have improved knowledge/safer sexual practices in target countries by 2015. The project was extended for another year in order to enable the Project team achieve more, due the slow start of the project which was attributed to the organisation going through a transition. During the project, period approximately 371 800 children were reached. The project had clearly defined standards for defining direct and indirect reach. In defining reach, the CSE pillars with key topics were developed as a guide for partner organisations to use whilst developing context specific training manuals.Direct reach was also defined as making sure that the child has been engaged for at least four hours of CSE activities and Learning for a period of 6 months.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
